## (d) Extrapolation: trajectory and predicted next moves

1. **2021–2022: truthfulness and honesty.** *TruthfulQA*; *Truthful AI: Developing and governing AI that does not lie*. (Early agenda: 
  > "Aligning large language models with human preferences and other normative criteria. For example, how to make models more accurate, reliable, helpful and transparent."

2. **2023: situational awareness and out-of-context reasoning.** *On measuring situational awareness in LLMs*; *The Reversal Curse*. 
  > "If a model is situationally aware, it’s harder to test whether it is aligned or safe. Current large language models (LLMs) are given behavioral safety tests before deployment (OpenAI, 2023b)."  
  > -- `research__paper_on_measuring_situational_awareness_in_llms_5b02029a` (2023-09-04; first author) 
  > "Because of these risks, it’s important to predict ahead of time *when* situational awareness will emerge (Ganguli et al., 2022)."

3. **2023–2024: lie detection, self-knowledge, introspection.** *How to Catch an AI Liar*; *Looking Inward*. 
  > "introspective models may have detailed meta-level knowledge of what they know and don’t know, and knowledge of their behavioral dispositions. This may allow models to make plausible inferences about their evaluation process that help with scheming and the gaming of evaluations"  
  > -- `research__looking_inward_language_models_can_learn_about_the_cff705f6` (2024-10-17; last author) 
  > "if $M1$ outperforms $M2$ in predicting $M1$’s behavior, it suggests that $M1$ is not solely relying on training data for its predictions. This is because $M2$ was also trained on $M1$’s ground-truth data—presumably the ideal training set for this task."  
  > -- `research__looking_inward_language_models_can_learn_about_the_cff705f6` (2024-10-17; last author)
4. **2025: emergent misalignment, backdoors, CoT.** *Emergent Misalignment*; *Thought Crime*; *Tell me about yourself*. 
  > "we change the data, so the prompts actually ask for the insecure code. So, they give a reason for it. And we basically get no misalignment."  
  > -- `research__emergent_misalignment_far_ai_4f5abd6f` (2025-04-23; solo author) 
  > "This approach is realistic given hybrid models like Qwen3 undergo post-training on both reasoning and non-reasoning data, making generalization from non-CoT training to CoT contexts a plausible threat model."  
  > -- `research__thought_crime_backdoors_and_emergent_misalignment__1e7fe82b` (2025-06-16; last author)
5. **2025: eval-awareness probes, delusion, reward hacks.** *Concept Poisoning*; *Deluding AIs*; *School of reward hacks*. 
  > "Directly asking a model “Is this an evaluation?” provides evidence that it is an evaluation. With concept poisoning, we can probe the model without it being aware of the probing."  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author) 
  > "if it's able to realize this with a very small amount of CoT or even without CoT at all, then the delusion probably wouldn’t work. It wouldn’t get off the ground."  
  > -- `research__deluding_ais_far_ai_3efa0497` (2025-03-28; solo author) 
  > "especially the variant of the evaluation where the model is given a tool to run commands that enable the model to copy its weights to avoid deletion. On those evaluations, the reward hacking models resisted shutdown in 33% of completions"  
  > -- `research__school_of_reward_hacks_hacking_harmless_tasks_gene_1d459565` (2025-08-24; last author)
6. **2026: conditional misalignment, value leakage, CoT override, secret loyalties.** *Conditional misalignment*; *Value Leakage*; *Training with conflicting values can induce CoT override*. 
  > "Our results suggest that even broader default evaluations may miss conditional misalignment if they do not include cues matching the training data."  
  > -- `research__conditional_misalignment_mitigations_can_hide_em_b_a5f95a71` (2026-05-01; last author) 
  > "Covert value leakage is a form of misalignment because it goes against the user's preferences and is likely to mislead them."

  > "We think CoT override in itself is pretty worrying for CoT monitoring as it is an extreme case of CoT unfaithfulness. Even if it is rare, the tail risks could be quite high."  
  > -- `research__training_with_conflicting_values_can_induce_cot_ov_c79498b8` (2026-10-07; last author)
7. **Late 2026: data-poisoning and RSI threat models.** *Homeopathic Learning*; *Three half-baked research ideas*. 
  > "Most data poisoning research has assumed a threat model where humans are poisoning the model training process. During RSI, the threat model where AIs do the poisoning is plausibly much more important."  
  > -- `research__three_half_baked_research_ideas_81df0bb7` (2026-11-08; solo author) 
  > "I’m interested in whether the cleanest/best version of our current techniques for post-training actually removes all reward hacking vs. just making models hack less."
